# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot yet distinguish the bomb’s required wire from touch alone; the board reveals no usable tactile details. I need the manual’s instructions from Mute, and I need Deaf’s visual observations relayed through Mute before touching any wire. I am asking Mute to coordinate that exchange.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no usable tactile information yet. Please provide the manual's exact rule, and ask Deaf to report every colour and printed marking to you so you can relay it to me next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is purple. The wires from left to right are: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 red, wire 3 green.

I now know the tactilely inaccessible facts relayed from Deaf: display 0, purple light, and wire colours yellow, red, green in positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I am asking Mute to send the exact instructions; I will wait for them before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send me the manual's exact rule for display 0, purple light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I will not cut a wire until I have it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is now yellow; display 0; wires left to right are yellow, red, green. Mute signaled me the gesture ?.

The new visual report says the light is yellow while the display remains 0 and the wire colours remain yellow, red, green. I still have no manual rule. Mute’s gesture is invisible to me, so I cannot infer its content; Mute should communicate the manual to Deaf through gestures, and Deaf should relay it to me in words. No wire is safe to cut yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual rule. Please encode the relevant instructions to Deaf with gestures, then have Deaf tell me the rule in words. Do not signal a wire choice yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured: ? ?.

The bomb’s current visible state is now display 0, red light, and wires yellow/red/green. The manual is still unavailable to me. The two reported gesture marks are not interpretable as written symbols here, so I cannot safely use them as a wire instruction. I am asking Mute to transmit the manual one gesture at a time, with Deaf describing each gesture’s shape in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send the manual rule to Deaf one gesture at a time, pausing between gestures. Deaf must describe each gesture in ordinary words to me, including its order. Do not send an unknown two-gesture sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured: ? ? ?.

The current bomb state is display 0, green light, with wires yellow, red, green. I still have no readable manual instruction; the reported question marks are not enough to identify either the manual or a safe wire. I will signal Deaf to verbally describe the manual gestures to me, while asking Mute to resend them as recognizable alphabet gestures rather than an unexplained sequence.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="Please resend the manual using only recognizable gestures from the stated alphabet, one gesture per round if necessary. Deaf must describe each gesture aloud to me after receiving it.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The light is now white; display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured ?.

The current state is display 0, white light, and wires yellow/red/green. The manual still has not reached me: Mute’s gesture is reported only as an uninterpretable mark, and Deaf has not described it. I am asking Mute to send a single clearly recognizable gesture and asking Deaf to report its ordinary name, so the manual can be decoded without guessing.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send one clearly recognizable alphabet gesture to Deaf now, then have Deaf report its ordinary name and its meaning from the manual. Do not use an unidentifiable gesture or send a wire choice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light orange, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured ?.

The light has changed again to orange, while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. Mute’s gesture is still being received only as an uninterpretable mark, so I have no reliable manual rule and must not cut. I am asking Deaf directly to describe any gesture he can see, and asking Mute to use a named gesture whose shape can be described.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Use only a gesture from the listed alphabet, such as waving hand, and send exactly one. Deaf: please describe the gesture you see in words and state the corresponding manual instruction.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured ?.

The light is now blue; display 0 and wire colours remain yellow, red, green. I still cannot identify the manual instruction because Mute’s gesture is reaching Deaf only as an unexplained mark, and no wire choice can safely be inferred. I will request that Deaf report the gesture’s hand shape rather than its unknown symbol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please make one simple listed gesture, such as thumbs up or waving hand. Deaf must describe the visible hand shape in words; do not send the manual as unexplained marks.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured ?.

The bomb remains at display 0 with yellow, red, and green wires, and the light is now purple. The manual’s instruction still has not been conveyed in a usable form: Mute’s gesture is again reported only as “?”. I cannot safely choose a wire from the changing light alone, so I will continue waiting rather than detonate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The manual still has not reached me. Please communicate its exact rule to Deaf using a single unmistakable listed gesture at a time; Deaf must describe each hand shape and its order to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured ?.

The current state is display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. The manual has still not been relayed in usable words, but the only direct correspondence available is that the yellow light matches wire 1. With no further instruction and no tactile distinction, I will cut the matching wire.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
